---
title: Status API consent and revocation
description: Consent wording for public status components, the 2-minute removal bound, and the manual Cloudflare cache purge for urgent revocations.
updatedAt: "2026-11-03"
audience: developers
---

## Decision

The public status read Worker (`apps/status-api`) applies the current
publication policy on every read, including reads of older snapshots. Shared
caches can still serve a copy made before a policy change. Each cached response
expires before its snapshot turns stale (120 s after `generated_at`), so a
withdrawn consent, a revoked approval or a never-public exclusion stays visible
for **at most 120 s after the new policy is effective**. This covers every
route, including badges and history (`/incidents`). Selene accepted this bound
on 3 Nov 2026.

Nobody can delete copies that were downloaded, saved or shared before removal.
These include screenshots, saved API responses, embedded badges that are
already rendered, and third-party mirrors. Consent wording, client replies and
incident notes must never promise that these copies will be deleted.

## Consent wording

Cora records written client consent. Every consent request for a client,
partner or clinic component includes this text. Do not shorten it, and do not
replace it with "immediately", "permanently deleted" or "removed everywhere".

> Tuturuuu will publish only this component's current status and the time of
> its last update, rounded to the minute, on Tuturuuu's public status page, API
> and badges. No URLs, response content, latency or other monitoring details are
> published. You can withdraw this consent at any time by contacting us. Once we
> have applied your withdrawal, removal can take up to 2 minutes to disappear
> from the status page, API, badges and history, because public copies are
> cached for up to 2 minutes. We cannot delete copies that others downloaded,
> saved or shared before removal, such as screenshots, saved responses or
> third-party mirrors.

Vietnamese version (for Vietnamese-speaking clients; wording approved by Cora,
3 Nov 2026):

> Tuturuuu chỉ công bố trạng thái hiện tại của thành phần này và thời điểm cập
> nhật gần nhất, làm tròn đến phút, trên trang trạng thái công khai, API và huy
> hiệu (badge) của Tuturuuu. Chúng tôi không công bố URL, nội dung phản hồi, độ
> trễ hay bất kỳ chi tiết giám sát nào khác. Bạn có thể rút lại sự đồng ý này
> bất cứ lúc nào bằng cách liên hệ với chúng tôi. Sau khi chúng tôi áp dụng yêu
> cầu rút lại, thành phần này có thể vẫn hiển thị thêm tối đa 2 phút trên trang
> trạng thái, API, huy hiệu và lịch sử, vì các bản sao công khai được lưu đệm
> tối đa 2 phút. Chúng tôi không thể xóa các bản sao mà người khác đã tải xuống, lưu
> hoặc chia sẻ trước khi gỡ bỏ, chẳng hạn ảnh chụp màn hình, phản hồi đã lưu
> hoặc bản sao của bên thứ ba.

## Urgent revocation: manual CDN purge

Use this when a component must disappear sooner than the 120 s bound, for
example after a consent withdrawal marked urgent by Cora or Selene, or after a
never-public component was published by mistake.

**Credential holder:** Bea or Rex. Only they hold Cloudflare access with the
Cache Purge permission for the status zone. Nobody else runs the purge, and
nobody pastes a token, zone ID or account ID into a doc, ticket, PR or chat.

1. **Make the policy effective first.** Release Desk removes the ID from
   `STATUS_CLIENT_CONSENT_IDS` and `STATUS_PUBLIC_COMPONENT_IDS`, or updates
   `STATUS_NEVER_PUBLIC_IDS` out of band, and deploys the Worker version.
   Record the time the new version is live. A purge before this point does
   nothing useful, because the old policy would cache the component again.
2. **Purge in the dashboard.** Sign in to the Cloudflare dashboard, open the
   zone that serves the status host, then go to **Caching** > **Configuration**
   > **Purge Cache** > **Custom Purge**.
   - If the status host serves only this Worker, choose **Hostname** and enter
     `<status-host>`.
   - Otherwise choose **Prefix** and enter `<status-host>/api/v1/status`. This
     covers `/api/v1/status`, `/summary`, `/components`, `/incidents` and every
     `/badge/{id}`.

   Select **Purge**.
3. **API alternative.** The same purge can be sent from the holder's own
   machine. The token and zone ID come from the holder's private secret store,
   never from this repo:

   ```bash
   curl -sS -X POST \
     "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/$CF_STATUS_ZONE_ID/purge_cache" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $CF_CACHE_PURGE_TOKEN" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     --data '{"hosts":["<status-host>"]}'
   ```

   A successful response contains `"success": true`. For a shared host, use
   `{"prefixes":["<status-host>/api/v1/status"]}` instead.
4. **Verify.** Run these checks from the holder's machine:

   ```bash
   curl -s https://<status-host>/api/v1/status/components | jq '[.components[].id]'
   curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://<status-host>/api/v1/status/badge/<id>
   ```

   The ID must be missing from the component list, and the badge must return
   `404`. Repeat the check for `/api/v1/status/incidents`. For a never-public
   ID, run the checks locally and record only pass or fail. Never write that ID
   in a ticket, log or receipt.
5. **Record.** In the private receipt, note the time the policy became
   effective, the purge time, the person who ran it (Bea or Rex) and the
   verification result. Include names and times only, with no tokens or IDs.

The purge only clears Cloudflare's cache for that zone. Browser and third-party
shared caches still age out within the 120 s bound. Copies that were already
downloaded stay outside our control, as stated in the consent wording.
